author: GamingBolt
description:
Although 2025 was a relatively slow year for Soulslikes, 2026 is bringing a bunch of them to our hands, and some of these new ones come with a lot of reasons for us to be absolutely delighted. 

From extraction RPGs to dungeon crawlers, there are a lot of interesting titles for Soulslike fans to try. Of course, it goes without saying that you're going to have to bring your best to each battle you fight lest you get summarily wrecked and sent back to the last point of safety. 

But to those who swear by the genre's merits, that's just part of the fun after all. It's going to be a fun year or two for fans of the genre, that's for sure.
title: 15 NEW Soulslike Games of 2026 And Beyond You NEED TO PLAY [PS5, XBOX SERIES X | S, PC, SWITCH 2]

author: GamingBolt
description:
It's evident that Resident Evil Requiem is a very different experience from the one on offer in Resident Evil Village. Ethan Winters’ search for his daughter relied a lot on the use of firearms to control enemy hordes in a more action-focused gameplay loop that made sense given the Village's size and scope. 

But Requiem has us getting close and personal with our protagonist duo, and the enemies they have to face down. That brings a whole lot of changes that make the new game a potent mix of the genre's best ideas. 

We take a look at some of the ways the upcoming horror game sets itself apart from the experiences that came before it even as it draws on them for inspiration.
title: Resident Evil Requiem vs. Resident Evil Village - 15 BIGGEST Differences You NEED TO KNOW

author: GamingBolt
description:
Highguard offers an extensive amount of microtransactions, but there's also a free Warbond-like battle pass that you can unlock items from using in-game currency (which is separate from the unlockable cosmetics for weapons and Wardens). 

It's par for the course in today's multiplayer sphere, except I received a measly 80 purpley doodahs after 40 minutes of play, and one item unlock costs 400. You'll be shocked to hear that I won't be spending another two hours and 40 minutes to amass more, even if there are other sources.

After all this, we come full circle and I ask once again. Who is Highguard for? What does it really offer that's unique in today's market, outside of combining several discordant competitive shooter mechanics into an abomination that's more boring than hideous?
title: Highguard Review - The Final Verdict
